items.title: Clyde Kerr Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 22, 2006
items.q: I mean in the beginning he would sound like Dizzy Gillespie and when he was hanging around with Charlie Parker and those guys.

ctx.x: That’s right. You have to learn how to deal with what you might have thought — I didn’t mean to do that but now I’m going to make it sound like I did.

Right. And that’s the thing, to learn how to recover and to react to your mistakes and that’s how we learn. We don’t learn from doing the same things over and over again. I’ve learned more from the mistakes I’ve made that has helped me to become a better teacher. Because I know what you’re going through and I know what you’re doing because I’ve done that so I can tell you what you need to do to kind of correct that or whatever. But it’s beautiful. I think Miles Davis’ style was more out of his weaknesses than his…
I know. Just seems like when you got into what he was doing he was on to something else.
